title: QBR Usage & Billing Worksheet — Token Spend, Rate Limits, Alerts
body:
Purpose and intended audience:
This worksheet is a customer-success-facing artifact to prepare for quarterly business reviews (QBRs) focused on usage and billing. Primary audience: CS account lead, solutions engineer, finance/business ops reviewer, and the customer technical owner.

How to use this doc:
- Fill in the data pulls for the QBR period (default: last 90 days).
- Highlight anomalies (spikes, unexpected throttles, runaway jobs).
- Provide clear recommendations tied to cost-savings and reliability actions.
- Export the two summary slides and the playbook snippets for operational handoff.

Section A: Executive summary (one paragraph)
- Topline usage trend: e.g., "Tokens up 42% QoQ due to batch embed job; 60% of tokens generated by 3 endpoints."
- Billing impact: e.g., "Billing rose from $18k/mo to $25.5k/mo; projected run rate without mitigation = $32k/mo."
- Risk callouts: persistent rate-limit events during peak hours, one customer job generating 30% of daily tokens.

Section B: Key metrics (fill values for the QBR range)
- Date range: ______ to ______
- Total token spend (input bearer billing units): ______ tokens / $ ______
- Average tokens per request: ______ tokens/request
- Requests per minute (avg / p95 / p99): avg: ______, p95: ______, p99: ______
- Peak concurrent request rate (RPS): ______
- Number of rate-limit / 429 events: ______ (count)
- Throttled unique API keys: ______
- Budget threshold consumption (current period): 0-50% / 50-70% / 70-90% / 90-100% (mark one)
- Unexpected long-running sessions (KV cache misses) count: ______
- Model mix (% of total tokens): model-a: __% , model-b: __% , open-llama-v2: __%

Section C: Data pulls and queries (recommended canonical queries)
- Token aggregation by day (pseudo-SQL):
  SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) as day, SUM(request_tokens+response_tokens) as total_tokens, COUNT(*) as requests
  FROM redwood_api_logs
  WHERE customer_id = 'CUST-123' AND ts BETWEEN '2025-11-15' AND '2026-02-15'
  GROUP BY day
  ORDER BY day;

- Rate-limit event query (example):
  SELECT ts, api_key, route, error_code, count(*) as events
  FROM redwood_error_logs
  WHERE customer_id='CUST-123' AND error_code='RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED' AND ts BETWEEN ...
  GROUP BY ts, api_key, route;

- Budget/commit reconciliation snippet (monthly):
  SELECT month, SUM(billed_amount) as billed, SUM(units) as units FROM billing_events WHERE customer_id='CUST-123' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;

Section D: Quick analysis helpers (formulas you can paste into the spreadsheet)
- Projected monthly run rate = (total_spend_in_period / days_in_period) * 30
- Overrun probability (simple) = (#days consumption > daily_budget / days_in_period) * 100 / days_in_period
- Sensitivity: tokens per active-user = total_tokens / active_users; to reduce cost by X% find required tokens reduction = total_tokens * X%

Section E: Observed anomalies (example entries you should populate)
- 2026-01-17: 03:00 UTC — 6x spike in tokens due to nightly batch embedding job; API key: embed-service; tokens = 18M (normal daily = 1.8M)
- 2026-02-02: 13:20–14:40 UTC — sustained 429s on route /v1/chat/stream; peak p99 latency increased; root cause: request fanout after a retry bug
- 2026-02-24: repeated preflight bursts from integration test environment during deploys; recommended to IP-block or add test-key

Section F: Recommendations (actionable & prioritized)
1) Short term (0–14 days):
   - Add budget alert thresholds at 70% and 90% (send to #cs-alerts and account owner email).
   - Temporarily raise rate limits for the integration test key to avoid false positives, but patch the retry logic on the client.
   - Throttle or schedule large batch jobs to off-peak windows (apply policy: off-peak window 02:00–06:00 UTC).
2) Medium term (2–6 weeks):
   - Enable prefix/KV caching on the chat endpoints for known high-frequency prompts (estimated savings 12–28% tokens).
   - Consider switching heavy embedding workloads to a lower-cost model variant or quantized variant when fidelity trade-off is acceptable.
   - Implement token-level sampling on analytics endpoints (sample 1:10) to cut ingestion tokens by ~90% for metrics pipelines.
3) Long term (quarter+):
   - Negotiate a Dedicated commit or Reserved capacity for predictable heavy-usage customers; use tiered commit to reduce unit cost by X%.
   - Add automated runbook that converts sustained daily spend > 120% of commit into an OOB pricing review with finance.

Section G: Playbook — "Budget alert (70% or 90%)"
Trigger: billing pipeline emits alert that cumulative spend for billing period >= threshold.
Immediate steps (CS engineer):
- Communicate: post short note to account Slack + #cs-alerts channel with subject: "[ALERT] CUST-123 hit 90% billing threshold"
  Template: "CUST-123 hit 90% of monthly budget ($X of $Y). Top contributors: embed-service (34%), chat-api (28%). Action: schedule 30-min call to review mitigation options."
- Pull live dashboard: tokens by endpoint, p95 latency, 429 count (last 24h).
- If pattern shows single-job runaway, propose immediate mitigations: kill job, apply temporary rate limit, or rollback deploy.
- If pattern is sustained growth, propose commit/discount or reserved capacity conversation and attach run rate forecast.
Escalation (if alert persists >48h or customer requests SLA): loop in AE + finance to discuss commit modification and invoice cadence.

Section H: Playbook — "Rate-limit spike / customer visible throttles"
Trigger: >50 429s in 1 hour impacting customer SLA or product features.
Immediate steps:
- Validate whether throttles are due to global RU caps, per-key quotas, or regional capacity (check allocation routing).
- Apply a temporary per-key quota increase if within safety limits and if customer is willing to accept overage exposure.
- If rate spike is due to misbehaving client, provide immediate client-side mitigations (backoff policy, jitter, idempotency tokens).
- Document root cause as ticket (JIRA) and attach logs + correlation ids.

Section I: Renewal & commit conversation notes (QBR talking points)
- Use run-rate baseline + mitigation scenarios: "If we patch batch jobs and enable caching, projected run-rate = $22k/mo (from $32k). With a 12-month committed capacity at $20k/mo equivalent, you get 10% discount + 99.9% SLA."
- Offer options: short-term overage protection window (30 days), mid-term reserved increment for peak hours, long-term dedicated pool.
- Prepare a 1-page appendix with modeled tiers (no nested doc; include 3 scenarios: base, optimized, committed).

Section J: Attachable artifacts for the QBR slide deck (copy/paste)
- Slide 1 (headline): "Usage & Billing — Last 90 days" bullets: total tokens, %QoQ, main drivers, action ask (approve commit / apply throttles).
- Slide 2 (deep dive): small table: endpoint | tokens | %total | recommended action.
- Slide 3 (playbook): quick steps for budget alert + rate-limit spike + renewal options.

Section K: Checklists before the QBR (tick boxes)
- [ ] Data exports for logs + billing (CSV) pulled and validated
- [ ] Top 10 endpoints by token use identified & annotated
- [ ] One-line root cause notes for each anomaly
- [ ] Playbook messages pre-drafted (Slack + email)
- [ ] Renewal scenarios modeled and attached

Appendix: Example Slack/email templates
- Slack (alert): "@channel FYI: CUST-123 has reached 90% of monthly budget ($27,900 of $31,000). Top contributors: embed-service (34%), chat-api (28%). CS lead @Ava: scheduling 30-min review. See dashboards: <link>"
- Email (to customer): Subject: "Usage threshold reached — quick sync?" Body: "Hi <Name>, We noticed consumption is approaching your monthly threshold. We've identified top contributors and prepared mitigation options (scheduling large jobs, model swap, reserved capacity). Can we schedule 30 minutes to review? Attaching a short run-rate forecast. — Ava, CS Lead"

Notes & provenance
- Data sources: billing_events table, redwood_api_logs, redwood_error_logs, console dashboards
- Owner of this doc: CS lead (owner field). Keep status = draft until validated with finance and product.
- Suggested exports: one CSV for daily tokens, one CSV for rate-limit events, one CSV for billing per invoice line.

Fields to fill (for QBR slide prep)
- Name of customer: ______
- Billing period: ______
- Total tokens: ______
- Run-rate (projected): $______
- Top-3 endpoints and tokens: 1) ______ 2) ______ 3) ______

End of worksheet.

Author notes: bundle this file with the QBR deck and the three CSV exports. Keep one version per quarter and append a short summary of actions taken (closed items) to the top of the next quarter's worksheet.
